{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_vrtx_011Ch7CxD7fhQn8CuSTBmoV9","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I fixed three rendering bugs in floating entities (sprites and upright sprites). One caveat first: I never saw the video. The file `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` doesn't exist in the container (the folder is empty), so I found these by reading and reasoning through the code, not by matching frames. The client builds, but I haven't run the game or any tests, so none of this has been checked visually.\n\n**1. Every `sprite` entity was drawn mirrored** (`irr/src/CBillboardSceneNode.cpp`)\nThe billboard put the right edge of the texture on the left of the quad and the left edge on the right. Any always-facing-camera sprite showed its picture flipped left-to-right, from every angle. I swapped the texture coordinates so they line up with the corners they belong to.\n\n**2. `upright_sprite` was mirrored when seen from behind** (`src/client/content_cao.cpp`, back face in `addToScene`)\nThe back face reused the front face's corner layout and only reversed the drawing order, so from behind the picture came out flipped. The back face now has its own layout, with texture left/right matching what you see from that side. Its sprite-sheet animation still lines up.\n\n**3. Sprites that show a different picture depending on viewing angle chose the wrong one** (`updateTexturePos`)\nThese sprites pick a frame by comparing the camera direction with the direction the entity faces. That code had two problems:\n- **Wrong turn direction:** it added the entity's yaw where it should subtract it. An entity that wasn't turned looked right, but a turned one showed the wrong side's frame, e.g. left and right swapped when turned 90°.\n- **Carried entities:** it only used the entity's own yaw. A sprite carried by another entity (like the one above the penguin) never accounted for its carrier turning, so its frame was wrong as the carrier walked its loop.\n\nIt now converts the camera direction into the entity's own frame. For a carried entity that uses the rendered world orientation (carrier plus attachment rotation); for a standalone one it uses the entity's yaw with the same sign the mesh rendering uses. The above/below frames use the same frame, so they're right however the entity is placed, turned or carried.\n\nTo confirm, run the yard scene again and check the sprites from the front, from behind, and while the penguin turns."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1887,"cache_read_input_tokens":43630,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1887,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":6,"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"e8483035-a674-467b-a867-9cd7a30c1a14","uuid":"5e314b15-e738-4d89-9956-2896c3d609d2","timestamp":"2026-11-16T20:04:48.284Z"}
